source: production/NOW.md JAFAR'S STANDING ORDER 2026-09-05 item 4; the 27 names pinned in production/queue/098-the-player-facing-systems-inventory-as-data.md
howToRead: area is the layer the system mostly lives in: moat (social memory, consequence, information), world (simulation and environment), player-facing (interface and input), content (authored material), studio (tools and process).

status is evidenced, never guessed. exists and partial each carry an evidence list of paths that resolve in this checkout; path#token means the token was found inside that file, which is the nearest thing to a call site provable without a compiler. absent carries no evidence, and the validator prints the words nothing measured for those.
phase names a row in ledger-v2/respec/roadmap-v2.md and means the phase whose gate this system has to clear, not the phase it was first touched in.
blocker is a queue number (queue-NNN), a decision id, or the word none. D1 is the open engine probe: every system built in Unity waits on it before more is invested.

systems.name: the Ledger notebook
systems.note: Panel built in code, bound to the Ledger key, opened and closed by the panel smoke test. What it SHOWS is D12's question, not this field's.

systems.name: HUD
systems.note: Clock, money and slot on one line plus the toast channel. The what-they-know HUD the roadmap names for wanted states is a separate thing and is not here.

systems.name: menus
systems.note: Front end built from code, no scenes and no prefabs; one options screen shared with the pause menu.

systems.name: controls
systems.note: Keyboard and mouse, nine rebindable actions, no two sharing a key. Pad support is the separate gamepad entry.

systems.name: camera
systems.note: One camera, third person, spring rig in Core and the wiring in the controller; the car takes the same camera over.

systems.name: first hour and tutorial
systems.note: First-morning onboarding is four diegetic toast lines fired on conditions, and Act I has its pressure points. There is no authored first hour judged as one.

systems.name: save and load
systems.note: Codec in Core, slots and quarantine in Game, and the SaveChaos harness runs inside verify so a broken round trip is red before commit.

systems.name: new game
systems.note: New game and Continue are both on the front screen, and Continue names whether a save exists.

systems.name: settings
systems.note: Plain-text settings.json next to the save, defaults survive a round trip, a corrupt file costs nothing.

systems.name: accessibility
systems.note: Three affordances shipped: text scale 80 to 150, colourblind-safe hues, captions including sounds. No pad remapping, no reduced motion, no audio-description pass, and nothing measures the set.

systems.name: subtitles
systems.note: Caption model in Core, bar in Game, created at boot; setting is 0 off, 1 speech, 2 speech and sounds.

systems.name: gamepad
systems.note: Only mouse and keyboard axes are read, there is no InputManager.asset in ProjectSettings, and the single gamepad mention is a comment about menu focus. Nothing measures pad play.

systems.name: pause
systems.note: Pause panel opens on the bound key and the smoke test asserts it opens, has words and gives the controls back.

systems.name: map and minimap
systems.note: Zero hits for minimap or a map panel anywhere in the scripts. Core/StreetMap.cs is the street network as sim data for walkers and cars, not a surface the player sees.

systems.name: inventory
systems.note: By design there is no grid and no bag: the Coat is the whole idea, and it is toggled by a key. The one screen Coat.cs says it should have does not exist, so this is partial and not exists.

systems.name: economy and trading
systems.note: Money, purses and dirty cash are wired across the Game layer. Trading is not: Core/Negotiation.cs is reached only from Core/Empire.cs and there are no prices, no trade surface and no shop.

systems.name: combat
systems.note: Violence, harm and standoffs are wired, but the ONLY call into Core/Combat from the Game layer is the stamina term the walk uses; the comment beside it says combat takes it over when it arrives. Phase 4's gate is combat called from live play.

systems.name: music
systems.note: A music bus plays a synthesised day and night pair and the adaptive layer model exists in Core. Audio.cs says it plainly: no authored score yet, and a score is a composer's job.

systems.name: SFX
systems.note: Every sound is synthesised at runtime unless a pack is dropped under StreamingAssets/Audio, and twelve Game files play through the funnel. Spare and diegetic by choice, not by omission.

systems.name: audio mix
systems.note: Buses, a per-bus voice budget, protected lines and square-root crowd gain. It was written, tested and unreachable once; the call sites in Audio.cs are what make this exists rather than absent.

systems.name: loading and streaming
systems.note: Assets load from a StreamingAssets pack when present and the curtain covers staged transitions. There is no loading screen and no streaming of world chunks: grep for loading in Bootstrap, AssetLibrary and ScreenCurtain returns nothing.

systems.name: failure states and autosave policy
systems.note: Autosave is policy and runs: the morning close saves quietly. The Fall is staged behind the curtain. Arrest is NOT a live failure state: CoatHost.Arrested has zero callers in the whole Game layer, named in Core/Homicide.cs as the cost of a lowercase bug.

systems.name: time and calendar display
systems.note: Day, hour, minute and slot are printed to the HUD every frame off the Core clock. Calendar events exist in the sim; a calendar the player can open does not.

systems.name: graphics settings including the local-LLM toggle
systems.note: Graphics half exists: two sliders on the options screen, preset and render scale 100/75/55. Grain is a live setting applied by FilmGrade with NO row on that screen. The local-LLM half is ABSENT, zero hits for any llm toggle in settings or options; the only live switch is an Anthropic API key panel on F2.

systems.name: credits and attributions
systems.note: The attribution ledger exists and is checked on every commit by verify. The in-game credits screen does not exist: the only two mentions in the scripts are comments.

systems.name: photo mode
systems.note: Zero hits for photo mode or a screenshot capture path in the scripts; the screenshot mentions are all about the studio's own stills. Nothing measured.

systems.name: feedback path
systems.note: The path that exists carries Jafar's messages from Telegram into the repo, and it has two named holes until queue 090. There is no in-game path by which a player reports anything.
